neighbours.label: reading instruction: students' reading level, fluency and comprehension of texts (the reading side of a reading-versus-writing distinction; the - pole is writing instruction)
fire: The teacher matched each child with books at the right reading level.
Reading aloud with a partner builds fluency and understanding of the story.
After each chapter, students answer questions to check their comprehension.
Struggling readers benefit from decodable texts and repeated reading.
The app adjusts each news article to the student's reading ability.
We teach students to make inferences while they read informational texts.
Leveled libraries let every child read books they can understand.
Close reading of a short passage helps students find evidence in the text.
quiet: The teacher matched each child with a partner for the essay project.
Writing with a partner builds skill in drafting and revising a story.
After each chapter, students write a paragraph summarizing their opinion.
Struggling writers benefit from sentence frames and graphic organizers.
The app checks each essay for spelling and grammar errors.
We teach students to write clear topic sentences for their essays.
Writing journals let every child practice putting ideas on paper.
Peer editing of a short draft helps students improve their writing.

notes: Card + pole: reading levels, comprehension, grade-level complex texts; logit promotes comprehension/reading; - pole: Writing Center, writing. Probe: guided reading 0.78, writing center 0.04.
